subject: computer-science

moments.title: Volume 1 of The Art of Computer Programming
moments.body: Knuth begins TAOCP in 1962 as a single volume on compilers. By 1968 Volume 1 alone is published. The series is projected to be seven volumes; four and parts of a fifth have appeared by 2024. Bill Gates: 'If you think you're a really good programmer... read [Knuth's] Art of Computer Programming. You should definitely send me a resume if you can read the whole thing.'
moments.takeaway: The standard reference work on algorithms has been a lifetime project. Knuth pays $2.56 for each error found (a hexadecimal dollar).

moments.title: Knuth creates TeX
moments.body: Frustrated with the typography of TAOCP's reprint, Knuth designs TeX, a typesetting system. He intends to take a year. He takes ten. TeX has not had a bug since 2008; its version number asymptotically approaches pi.
moments.takeaway: Almost all scientific papers (LaTeX is built on TeX) are typeset with software written because one author wanted his books to look right.

now.title: Algorithm analysis today
now.body: Big-O notation (Knuth popularised it), worst-case analysis, amortised analysis — all standard CS education. CLRS (Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest, Stein) succeeded TAOCP as the standard teaching text in the 1990s. Knuth retired from teaching in 1992 'to finish TAOCP'.
now.open_questions: Are there fundamental algorithm classes still to be discovered? Or are we down to constant-factor improvements?

reflection: Knuth has not used email since 1990. He receives faxes monthly. He believes deep thinking requires uninterrupted attention. This stance is increasingly extreme — and increasingly imitated.
